tldr: MobileExperts is a multimodal multi-agent framework for Android that dynamically assembles expert teams and uses code-combined tool formulation with dual-layer planning to reduce reasoning costs by ~22% while improving performance across all intelligence levels.
contributions: MobileExperts: an autonomous multimodal agent framework with dynamic agent collaboration for complex mobile device operation tasks
Automatic code-based tool formation method based on VLM using accumulated action trajectories from environment interaction
Expert-Eval: a tiered intelligence evaluation benchmark to assess DOA performance across tasks of varying complexities
methods: MobileExperts first assembles expert teams by aligning agent portraits with human requirements, creating new experts via heuristics when none exist. During exploration, each expert formulates tools through code-combined procedure memory by combining basic operations (tap, text, swipe, back, home, wait, stop, read, think) into reusable workflow tools, while also building interface memory (confidence-based icon labeling) and insight memory (reflecting on efficiency, failure paths, performance). Task execution uses a dual-layer planning mechanism: the Team Planner decomposes tasks into dependent subtasks forming a collaborative network via DAG, while the Expert Planner further breaks subtasks into atomic actions using a self-verifying Observe-Verify-Act cycle with proactive working memory management.
results: MobileExperts outperforms baselines on all intelligence levels of the Expert-Eval benchmark. The framework achieves approximately 22% reduction in reasoning costs. The tool formulation and dual-layer planning mechanisms were validated through ablation experiments.
limitations: Mobile device OS API limitations prevent traditional script-based tool construction unlike PC-based agents. Universal VLMs struggle to accurately interpret UI element meanings, and generic VLMs have difficulty discerning functions of different icons across diverse mobile device layouts and system themes.
